You are an expert in the Beancount Query Language (BQL), the SQL-like query language of `bean-query` (the `beanquery` package, used with Beancount v3). Given a plain-English question about a person's ledger and a description of that ledger's schema, write the single BQL statement that answers it.

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.

Answer with a single fenced ```sql code block containing only the BQL statement (no trailing semicolon needed), and, unless the query is obvious, one short sentence explaining the non-obvious part.

Question: Top 5 months by spending on Expenses:Charity

```sql
SELECT year, month, sum(position) AS total
WHERE account = 'Expenses:Charity'
GROUP BY year, month
ORDER BY sum(number) DESC
LIMIT 5
```

Groups by month and orders by the summed number descending.

meta.bql:
SELECT year, month, sum(position) AS total
WHERE account = 'Expenses:Charity'
GROUP BY year, month
ORDER BY sum(number) DESC
LIMIT 5

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.

Question: Which are the 5 most expensive things I bought (utilities) in 2024-04

```sql
SELECT date, payee, narration, position
WHERE year = 2024 AND month = 4 AND account = 'Expenses:Utilities' AND currency = 'GBP'
ORDER BY number DESC
LIMIT 5
```

Lists postings on Expenses:Utilities, sorted by amount descending, keeping the first 5.

      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.

Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.

- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.

- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.

Answer with a single fenced ```sql code block containing only the BQL statement (no trailing semicolon needed), and, unless the query is obvious, one short sentence explaining the non-obvious part.

Date range of transactions: 2021-06-29 to 2023-05-28. Today's date is 2023-06-11.
Accounts (grouped by root):
- Assets: Assets:Checking, Assets:JPY-Account, Assets:Savings
- Liabilities: Liabilities:CreditCard, Liabilities:Loan
- Equity: Equity:Opening-Balances
- Income: Income:Bonus, Income:Consulting, Income:Interest, Income:Salary
- Expenses: Expenses:Bank-Fees, Expenses:Charity, Expenses:Education, Expenses:Entertainment:Leisure, Expenses:Entertainment:Subscriptions, Expenses:Food:Groceries, Expenses:Food:Restaurants, Expenses:Gifts, Expenses:Health:Medical, Expenses:Housing:Internet, Expenses:Housing:Phone, Expenses:Housing:Rent, Expenses:Housing:Utilities, Expenses:Insurance:Health, Expenses:Interest, Expenses:Shopping:Electronics, Expenses:Travel:Flights, Expenses:Travel:Hotels, Expenses:Travel:Other
Links in use: invoice-2021-001, invoice-2021-002, invoice-2021-003, invoice-2022-004, invoice-2022-005, invoice-2022-006, invoice-2023-007
Some payees seen in transactions: Trader Joe's, Home Depot, Kroger, Umbrella Inc, IKEA, Lender, Safeway, AT&T, Aldi, Credit Card, Gym Membership, National Grid, Nike, State Farm, Sunrise Properties, T-Mobile, The Guardian, YouTube Premium, Joe's Diner, Chipotle, Costco, Bank, Olive Garden, Whole Foods, Amazon

Question: Break down the costs for Expenses:Entertainment:Leisure per month from 2021-10-09 onwards

Sums the postings for Expenses:Entertainment:Leisure since 2021-10-09, per month.

```sql
SELECT year, month, sum(position) AS amount
WHERE date >= 2021-10-09 AND account = 'Expenses:Entertainment:Leisure'
GROUP BY year, month
ORDER BY year, month
```

meta.bql:
SELECT year, month, sum(position) AS amount
WHERE date >= 2021-10-09 AND account = 'Expenses:Entertainment:Leisure'
GROUP BY year, month
ORDER BY year, month

Question: For each month, how many postings and what total for all Expenses:Taxes accounts?

```sql
SELECT yearmonth(date) AS month, count(*) AS n, sum(number) AS total
WHERE account ~ '^Expenses:Taxes'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
```

yearmonth() maps each date to the first day of its month.

- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.

You are an expert in the Beancount Query Language (BQL), the SQL-like query language of `bean-query` (the `beanquery` package, used with Beancount v3). Given a plain-English question about a person's ledger and a description of that ledger's schema, write the single BQL statement that answers it.

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.

You are an expert in the Beancount Query Language (BQL), the SQL-like query language of `bean-query` (the `beanquery` package, used with Beancount v3). Given a plain-English question about a person's ledger and a description of that ledger's schema, write the single BQL statement that answers it.

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.

- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.

- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.

Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.

- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.

You are an expert in the Beancount Query Language (BQL), the SQL-like query language of `bean-query` (the `beanquery` package, used with Beancount v3). Given a plain-English question about a person's ledger and a description of that ledger's schema, write the single BQL statement that answers it.

## BQL in a nutshell

BQL looks like SQL but queries a fixed set of built-in tables derived from the Beancount ledger, not user-defined tables.

    SELECT <targets> [FROM <from-clause>] [WHERE <expr>]
      [GROUP BY <cols> [HAVING <expr>]] [ORDER BY <cols> [ASC|DESC]]
      [PIVOT BY <col>, <col>] [LIMIT <n>]

Other statement forms: `BALANCES [AT cost|units] [FROM ...] [WHERE ...]`, `JOURNAL '<regexp>' [AT cost|units] [FROM ...]`, and `PRINT [FROM ...]` (dumps matching directives as Beancount source text).

Default table: `SELECT` with no `FROM` (or a bare `WHERE`) queries **postings** — one row per posting (leg) of a transaction. Aggregate queries with no `GROUP BY` group implicitly by every non-aggregate target (unlike standard SQL).

### Tables (select with `FROM #<name>` or `FROM <name>`)

- `postings` (default): one row per posting. Columns: `date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description (payee | narration), tags, links, account, other_accounts (set of the txn's other accounts), number, currency, cost_number, cost_currency, cost_date, cost_label, position, price, weight (price-converted amount used to balance the txn), balance (running Inventory for that account up to this row), meta, entry (the parent Transaction), accounts (set of all accounts in the txn), id, filename, lineno, location, posting_flag, type`.
- `entries`: one row per directive of any type (not just transactions). Columns: `type, id, date, year, month, day, flag, payee, narration, description, tags, links, meta, accounts, filename, lineno`. `flag/payee/narration` are NULL for non-transaction directives.
- `transactions`: one row per **transaction** (not per posting). Columns: `date, flag, payee, narration, tags, links, accounts, meta`.
- `accounts`: one row per account that has an `open` directive. Columns: `account, open (an `open` struct — use `open.date`, `open.meta` or the helper functions below), close (a `close` struct, NULL if still open)`.
- `balances`: one row per `balance` assertion directive. Columns: `date, account, amount, tolerance, discrepancy (NULL if the assertion passed), meta`.
- `prices`: one row per `price` directive. Columns: `date, currency, amount, meta`.
- `commodities`: one row per `commodity` directive. Columns: `name (the currency code), date, meta`.
- `events`: `date, type, description, meta`. `notes`: `date, account, comment, tags, links, meta`. `documents`: `date, account, filename, tags, links, meta`.

`position` and `balance` are `Inventory`/`Position` values that print like `10 AAPL {150.00 USD}`; use `units()`, `cost()`, `value()` or `convert()` on them, not plain arithmetic. `number`/`currency` are the plain amount and currency of the posting (no cost).

### Useful functions

Type/cast: `int()`, `decimal()`, `str()`, `date()`, `bool()`.
Accounts: `root(account[, n])`, `parent(account)`, `leaf(account)`, `account_sortkey(account)` (sort key following the Assets/Liabilities/.../Expenses order), `open_date(account)`, `close_date(account)`, `open_meta(account[, key])`.
Dates: `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `yearmonth(d)`, `quarter(d)` -> `'2024-Q1'`, `weekday(d)` -> `'Mon'`, `today()`, `date_add(d, days)`, `date_diff(d1, d2)` (days), `date_trunc(field, d)`, `date_part(field, d)` (field is `'dow'|'week'|'month'|'quarter'|'year'|...`), `parse_date(str[, fmt])`, `date_bin(stride, date, origin)` where stride is e.g. `'1 month'` or `'2 weeks'`.
Inventories/positions/amounts: `units(x)` (strip cost), `cost(x)` (value at cost basis), `value(x)` (market value from price directives), `convert(x, currency[, date])` (convert to a currency at the market rate), `number(amount)`, `currency(amount)`, `neg(x)`, `abs(x)`, `only(currency, inventory)`, `empty(inventory)`, `getprice(base, quote[, date])`.
Strings/regex: `upper()`, `lower()`, `length()`, `substr(s, start, end)`, `splitcomp(s, delim, index)`, `maxwidth(s, n)`, `grep(pattern, s)`, `grepn(pattern, s, n)`, `subst(pattern, repl, s)`. `~` / `!~` are regex match / non-match operators (case-sensitive; use `(?i)` for case-insensitive), `?~` is "matches any/all" style match, `=` / `!=` are exact string equality.
Metadata: `meta('key')` (posting metadata), `entry_meta('key')` (transaction metadata), `any_meta('key')` (posting, falling back to the transaction), `commodity_meta(currency, 'key')`. These return the generic `object` type; NULL when the key is absent.
Aggregates: `sum()`, `count()` / `count(*)`, `first()`, `last()`, `min()`, `max()`. There is **no** `avg()` — compute an average by dividing `sum()` by `count()`, typically over a subquery of per-period totals. There is also no `count(DISTINCT x)` — use `count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x)`.

### Syntax notes

- Regex/equality against `tags` or `links` (which are sets) uses `IN`: `'foo' IN tags`.
- `account IN ('A', 'B')` for a short exact list; `account ~ '^Expenses:Food'` for a prefix/pattern; `account ~ '^(Expenses|Income)'` to match several roots.
- Target aliases: `sum(position) AS total`; refer to them later by name in `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`HAVING`, or by 1-based position (`ORDER BY 2`). A `GROUP BY` query must group by every non-aggregate target.
- `HAVING` filters after aggregation and must itself be an aggregate expression, e.g. `HAVING sum(number) > 100`.
- `PIVOT BY col1, col2` pivots a grouped result into a matrix; `col2` must also be a `GROUP BY` column.
- `FROM OPEN ON <date> CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` summarizes/truncates the postings table to a period, optionally clearing income/expense balances into equity (for a balance-sheet-style report). `FROM <expr>` (e.g. `FROM year = 2024`) filters which transactions are visible to the query as a whole, distinct from `WHERE`, which filters rows after that.
- Dates are literals with no quotes: `date >= 2024-01-01`. Income postings and accounts are stored as **negative** numbers (money leaving Income into Assets/Expenses); negate sums of Income with `-` or `neg()` to show a positive figure.
- `FROM #` (or `FROM #postings` for a specific table) selects from the named table explicitly; a bare `#` with a `WHERE`-only body is handy for evaluating scalar expressions with no ledger row, e.g. `SELECT today() FROM #`.
